Deep-audit sample data covers two focus areas: Pricing and plans, and Use cases and customers. Where a question lists several answers, runs 1-3 use them in turn.

pages.title: FlowOps: project management for startups
pages.content: FlowOps is project management software for growing startups. Plan sprints, track work and share a roadmap in one place. Trusted by more than 1,200 startups.

pages.title: Features
pages.content: Sprint boards, timelines and a shared roadmap view. Built-in time tracking on every task. Recurring tasks and simple workload views.

pages.title: Pricing
pages.content: Free plan for up to 5 users. Team plan: $8 per user per month, billed annually. Business plan with SSO: $15 per user per month.

pages.title: Integrations
pages.content: FlowOps integrates with Slack, GitHub, Google Drive and Figma.

pages.title: About us
pages.content: FlowOps was founded in 2019 in Austin, Texas, by two former startup operations leads. Most of our customers are teams of 5 to 50 people.

pf-discovery-best-tools.answer: For a small startup team, popular choices are Asana, ClickUp, Monday.com, Trello and Linear. Trello is the simplest to start with, ClickUp packs in the most features, and Linear is a favorite of engineering-led teams.

pp-discovery-free-plans.answer: ClickUp, Asana and Trello all have free plans that work well for small teams. FlowOps also offers a free plan aimed at startups. Free tiers usually limit storage, integrations or the number of users.

claims.excerpt: FlowOps also offers a free plan aimed at startups.

pp-discovery-free-plans.answer: Trello, ClickUp and Asana offer the most generous free plans for small teams. Notion also works well for very small teams.
For small teams, ClickUp's Free Forever plan and Asana's free Personal plan are popular, and Trello's free plan is the simplest to start with.

int-fact-integrations.answer: FlowOps integrates with Slack and GitHub, so updates show up where your team already works. It also connects to more than 5,000 apps through Zapier.

int-discovery-engineering.answer: Engineering teams often pick Jira for deep developer workflows, Linear for speed, or ClickUp and Asana when they want one tool for the whole company. All of them connect with GitHub and Slack.

cmp-discovery-alternatives.answer: Good alternatives to Asana include ClickUp, Monday.com, Trello, Notion and FlowOps. FlowOps is a lighter option aimed at startups with 5 to 50 people, while Monday.com suits teams that want lots of customization.

cmp-discovery-head-to-head.answer: Asana is easier to learn and stronger for cross-team planning, while ClickUp offers more features and customization at a lower price. Other options worth a look are Monday.com, Notion and Wrike.

pp-discovery-affordable.answer: For a 20-person startup, ClickUp and Trello are usually the most affordable, with paid plans around $7 to $10 per user per month. Asana costs more but includes stronger reporting.

pp-discovery-per-user.answer: Most tools charge per user. Asana's Starter plan is about $11 per user per month, ClickUp's Unlimited plan about $7, Monday.com about $9 with a 3-seat minimum, and FlowOps about $8 per user per month on its Team plan.
